To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the annihilation of two pseudoscalar mesons into two vector mesons requires the existence of a scalar meson, that this scalar meson is an elementary particle, that this particle lies on a Regge trajectory, and that the Regge trajectory is a moving Regge pole.
The annihilation amplitude for the reaction π + π −  → two vector mesons is dominated by the exchange of a Regge trajectory with the quantum numbers of the elementary scalar mesons.
the scalar meson is a Regge pole, the leading singularity is a Regge cut, and the Regge pole is a Reggeon.

the study of Regge poles in the π + π − annihilation amplitude into two vector mesons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the elementary scalar mesons are Regge poles.
the existence of elementary scalar mesons is a direct consequence of parity conservation and of rotational symmetry.
the elementary scalar mesons lie on Regge poles, which are the only singularities allowed by the symmetries of the theory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the existence of the scalar meson is a necessary consequence of the Regge poles in the vector-vector amplitude.
the Regge-pole model, which was originally developed for mesons and baryons, can be applied also to scalar mesons, and the elementary scalar mesons are Regge poles.
, in the scalar-vector field theory with elementary scalar mesons, the annihilation amplitude is dominated by a Regge pole with a mass of the order of the mass of the scalar meson.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the existence of a scalar meson triplet in the ππ → two vector meson amplitude, which is a consequence of parity conservation and rotational invariance, is independent of the dynamics.
